To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured spin echoes and deduced a spin coherence time of up to 2.8 us for free two dimensional electrons in a silicon based quantum well.

the spin coherence time of free two-dimensional (2D) electrons in Si/SGe quantum wells is limited by momentum scattering and that this mechanism can be eliminated by confining the electrons to the nondegenerate ground state of a dot.

the spin coherence time for free two-dimensional electrons can be increased by more than an order of magnitude by reducing their temperature and that the decoherence can be explained in terms of momentum-dependent Rashba fields.

the development of new materials, structures and devices for quantum information processing and the investigation of their physical properties.
spin manipulation of free two dimensional electrons in silicon.
understanding the spin coherence of free 2D electrons in Si/SGe quantum wells and with developing a quantum dot structure for spin qubits in Si/SiGex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin coherence times of free two-dimensional electron gases in semiconducting quantum wells can be significantly longer than previously believed.
we have demonstrated a spin coherence time of 3 mus, which is comparable to the best values reported for GaAs quantum wells.
the spin coherence of two-dimensional electrons in a Si/SGe quantum well is limited to 3 mus, and that the decoherence is dominated by fluctuating Rashba fields caused by momentum scattering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the spin of free electrons can be manipulated in a semiconductor quantum well, and that the spin decoherence can be explained by the momentum scattering.
we have measured spin echo decays of free electrons confined in a 2DEG in Si/Si-Ge quantum wells.
we are the first to measure spin echoes in free two-dimensional electrons and we have identified the dominant mechanism for spin decoherence in this material system.

the spin coherence of free electrons in semiconducors can be manipulated and extended to mus time scales.
